title: POC Weekly Sync - Quality Eval
summary: Weekly POC sync to review evaluation results from prompt sets A/B, inspect regressions flagged by the analyzer, discuss guardrail false positives, and agree next steps for tuning and benchmark runs. Customer is leaning toward dedicated capacity if latency stays under target but wants answers on encryption/KMS and SOC2 artifacts.
action_items: Priya Shah (Redwood SE): Run regression suite with updated prompt set B and return summary by 2026-03-11

transcript:
Header:
Date/Time: 2026-03-04 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Chris (Galaxy PM), Maria (Galaxy Eng), Jordan (Galaxy ML)

Summary (auto): quick review of weekly quality eval, regressions flagged, and prioritize tuning.

[00:00] Alex: Hey team, thanks for joining. quick check — can everyone hear okay?
[00:05] Chris: Yep, loud and clear, thanks.
[00:12] Priya: Cool. I'll share my screen in a sec, but first wanted to recap what we ran this week — prompts A and B across 1k samples, scoring rubric was 0-5 on relevance, hallucination, and instruction-following.
[00:28] Jordan: Just to clarify, those 1k were from the support ticket subset, right? Not full triage.
[00:34] Priya: Correct, support tickets only — we wanted the higher-signal subset to iterate faster.
[00:41] Maria: We also added the new guardrail rule for PHI masking, saw a few false positives on dates.
[00:48] Priya: Yeah saw that — the PHI detector mis-labeled some iso dates as PHI, might be a tokenizer edge-case or the regex was too broad.
[00:56] Alex: Ok perfect. Priya, can you walk the team through the top regressions?
[01:02] Priya: Sure. I'm pulling up the regression dashboard... okay first, overall accuracy delta between A and B: prompt B increased instruction-following by about 6%, but we saw a 3.5% increase in hallucination score on long context items (>1,000 tokens).
[01:22] Chris: 1,000 tokens — that's slightly above our usual live context, right? Our current UI cuts at ~800.
[01:29] Jordan: Right, most sessions are under 800 but some case escalations hit larger contexts. The KV cache behavior matters there.
[01:36] Priya: Exactly — we suspect KV caching / prefix cache misses are amplifying generation drift on longer sequences; runtime logs show a couple of prefix mismatch warnings, transcribed as "K V cash" in the debug.
[01:50] Maria: Is that something on the runtime side or the prompt design?
[01:54] Priya: A bit of both. Prompt B alters the instruction ordering which interacts with the KV cache warm-up pattern; on our side we can suggest a small reordering to reduce cache churn and also enable a short-lived warm prefix cache policy for the POC.
[02:10] Alex: On the business side Chris, you mentioned latency goals — remind me what your target SLO is for this flow?
[02:16] Chris: We want 95th percentile under 420ms for short queries (<=300 tokens). If we need dedicated to reach it that's okay, but cost has to be reasonable.
[02:26] Alex: Understood — we'll include a cost estimate for a 3-month dedicated trial with autoscaling and burst capacity.
[02:33] Jordan: Back on quality, there were a couple of edge-case label flips — examples 141, 372 where the model inserted a speculative diagnosis. Those are in the spreadsheet; labeling team marked as high severity.
[02:46] Priya: I pulled the examples — I can run a targeted guardrail patch: strengthen the 'no clinical inference' instruction and add a rejection template. That should reduce speculative outputs.
[02:56] Maria: Great — but we were worried about false positives where the model correctly redacts PII but then uses the rejection template too aggressively and drops helpful context.
[03:06] Priya: Good point. We can tune the threshold on the guardrail classifier — move from .5 to .65 for this class and run the evaluation again to measure precision/recall tradeoff.
[03:17] Chris: Do we have ROC curves from last week?
[03:20] Priya: I have them — uploading to the drive now, link in the chat. (link: https://shared.redwood/g/galaxy/guardrails)
[03:28] Alex: On compliance — Maria, you had questions about KMS and audit logs. We have SOC 2 documentation and KMS integration notes in the security pack I'll send after the call.
[03:40] Maria: Yes please. Also need to confirm whether keys can be customer-managed in the private deployment.
[03:46] Priya: For Private we support BYOK via customer KMS/HSM; for Dedicated we can offer tenant-level KMS integration — I'll include the architecture notes.
[03:55] Jordan: One more technical question — when you talk about quantized variants, are we comparing int8 runs only or do you have newer quant schemes? Some of our models are sensitive to fp16 drops.
[04:06] Priya: We're testing both int8 and newer 4-bit quant profiles; initial A/B used the 4-bit profile on prompt B which likely caused the hallucination bump on long contexts. For critical flows we suggest fp16 or a tuned 4-bit profile with per-layer calibration.
[04:22] Chris: So for the POC, recommended path is keep fp16 for long-context cases, and use tuned 4-bit for short sessions to save cost?
[04:29] Priya: Exactly, that's the hybrid we recommend. Also smart routing can send long-context requests to fp16 nodes.
[04:36] Alex: Let's talk about scoring and rubric alignment — Jordan, you mentioned labeler disagreement. How much inter-rater variance did we see?
[04:43] Jordan: About 12% overall disagreement on the hallucination bin, plus some confusion on partial answers — label instructions might not be strict enough.
[04:50] Maria: We need a tighter rubric, especially for ambiguous cases. Can Redwood help create an adjudication workflow?
[04:55] Priya: Yes — we can provide a template and a small script to surface high-disagreement examples for adjudication. I'll attach that.
[05:03] Chris: On regressions, is there an automated alerting we can turn on when a prompt set drops below a baseline?
[05:09] Priya: We have regression alerts in Redwood Optimize — can set thresholds on any metric and have daily digest emails. We can also hook into your Slack.
[05:16] Alex: Great. Any blockers from the customer's side for the next run?
[05:19] Maria: We need to clean the label CSV and confirm access for Redwood to the test environment. Security will want a minimal access role.
[05:27] Alex: Noted — we'll need a service account with read-only test access. Priya, do you want the env details?
[05:33] Priya: Yes please — and include sample logs so I can validate KV cache warnings.
[05:37] Jordan: We'll anonymize logs, remove PHI, and share a 2GB sample.
[05:42] Priya: Perfect.
[05:45] Chris: Quick question about pricing — can you do a committed monthly for Dedicated at a reduced rate? We'd probably do a 3-month pilot.
[05:53] Alex: Yes, we can provide a pilot pricing sheet; I'll include burst rules and overage caps in the quote.
[05:59] Maria: One last thing — do you have any recommendations for prompt engineering that reduced regression risk earlier?
[06:05] Priya: Two things we found useful: explicit 'do not speculate' tokens at top-of-prompt, and a short canonical context window that we always include to anchor the response. Also consistent instruction ordering — small changes cause large shifts with KV cache.
[06:20] Jordan: We'll try the anchor context and rerun.
[06:23] Priya: Cool. I'll schedule the regression run tonight and send results by Thursday.
[06:28] Alex: Okay let's recap next steps...
[06:31] Alex: Priya will run the regression with prompt B tweaks and threshold change on guardrail.
[06:36] Alex: Jordan will share label CSV and the sample logs.
[06:39] Alex: Maria will confirm service account details for read-only test access.
[06:43] Alex: I'll send the pricing/security pack. Follow-up sync 2026-03-11 same time.
[06:50] Chris: Sounds good, thanks everyone.
[06:53] Priya: Thanks all.
[07:00] End of meeting

Notes: Transcript has occasional ASR artifacts ("K V cash" for KV cache), basic filler words retained to reflect real meeting pace. Links referenced: guardrails ROC (https://shared.redwood/g/galaxy/guardrails), security pack draft (to be sent).
